title: Solubility equilibria, Ksp, common ion (AP)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EQ05#t3 term and clue written for the game; EQ05#t2 term and clue written for the game; EQ05#t4 term and clue written for the game; EQ05#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EQ05#N.4, EQ05#N.6, EQ05#N.9, EQ05#N.11, EQ05#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Saturated solution
items.clue: Mixture with excess solid in which ions leave the solid and rejoin it at equal rates.

items.label: Molar solubility
items.clue: The amount of a solid, symbol s, dissolved per unit volume once no more will dissolve.

items.label: Common-ion effect
items.clue: Less BaSO₄ dissolves in Na₂SO₄(aq) than in pure water, because SO₄²⁻ is already there.

items.label: Solubility product
items.clue: Equilibrium constant for a solid dissolving, e.g. [Ba²⁺][SO₄²⁻], with the solid left out.

questions.stem: The hypothetical salt MX₂ dissolves according to the equation MX₂(s) ⇌ M²⁺(aq) + 2 X⁻(aq). At 25°C, Ksp for MX₂ is 4.0 × 10⁻⁹. What is the molar solubility of MX₂ in water at 25°C?
questions.explanation: [M²⁺] = s and [X⁻] = 2s, so Ksp = 4s³. s³ = 1.0 × 10⁻⁹ and s = 1.0 × 10⁻³ M.

questions.stem: The hypothetical salt AB dissolves according to the equation AB(s) ⇌ A⁺(aq) + B⁻(aq). At 25°C, Ksp for AB is 25. Which statement about AB at 25°C is correct?

options.text: It is soluble, with a molar solubility of 5.0 M
It is soluble, with a molar solubility of 25 M
It is slightly soluble, like all salts that have a Ksp
It dissolves without limit, since its Ksp is above 1

questions.explanation: For a 1 : 1 salt, Ksp = s², so s = √25 = 5.0 M. Ksp > 1 corresponds to a soluble salt.

questions.stem: The hypothetical salt MX₂ dissolves according to the equation MX₂(s) ⇌ M²⁺(aq) + 2 X⁻(aq), with Ksp = 3.2 × 10⁻¹¹ at 25°C. What is the molar solubility of MX₂ at 25°C in a 0.020 M solution of NaX, a soluble salt?

Solid CaF₂ is in equilibrium with its saturated solution: CaF₂(s) ⇌ Ca²⁺(aq) + 2F⁻(aq). HF is a weak acid. A small amount of HNO₃(aq) is added at constant temperature, and solid CaF₂ remains. Which statement correctly describes [Ca²⁺] after equilibrium is re-established, and why?

options.text: It is higher, because adding acid increases the value of Ksp for CaF₂
It is unchanged, because Ksp for CaF₂ is a constant at this temperature
It is higher, because H₃O⁺ converts F⁻ to HF, so that more CaF₂ dissolves
It is lower, because the added H₃O⁺ shifts the equilibrium toward solid CaF₂

questions.explanation: F⁻ is the conjugate base of the weak acid HF. Removing F⁻ shifts the equilibrium toward dissolving, so [Ca²⁺] rises while Ksp stays the same.

questions.stem: Silver chloride has Ksp = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ at 25 °C. What is its molar solubility in 0.10 M NaCl(aq) at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: [Cl⁻] ≈ 0.10 M, so Ksp = s × 0.10 and s = 1.8 × 10⁻⁹ M. That is about 7500 times less than in pure water.
